text:
irina: Heads-up — saw intermittent end-to-end stalls on multi-GPU inference after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. Repro on CI with --use-cuda-graphs enabled.

sam: repro steps? flaky locally or CI-only?

irina: CI job: python -m perf.run --model llama-2-13b --tp=2 --pp=1 --batch-size=8 --seq-len=512 --use-cuda-graphs. Happens ~1/30 runs, presents as a 30-200ms stall in the middle of generation, then recovers.

priya: do we have nvprof/nvtx trace? sounds like comm/compute overlap is lost and NCCL waits spike.

irina: attached NVTX timeline cropped: "GPU0: compute kernels -> cudaGraph replay -> a long gap -> NCCL allreduce -> compute resumes". NCCL latency during stall: ~45ms vs normal ~3-4ms.

alex: two hypotheses: 1) cudaGraph capture recorded streams that now include operations from KV prefetch (non-capturable stream) so replay serializes, 2) kernel selection change altered seq length grouping so one rank picks a different fused kernel that forces sync.

sam: interesting — last week we changed batching heuristics to pack variable seq lengths more aggressively; that could change kernel launches. If one tensor-parallel shard uses a new kernel variant requiring a different workspace allocation, that might insert a sync.

priya: i pulled profiler (nsight systems) from a failed run. The trace shows cudaGraph::launch on stream 2, then an event recorded on stream 7 by kv-prefetch, then ncclAllReduce is launched on stream 2 but waits on that event. Because the event was recorded on a non-capturable stream, during cudaGraph replay the event is not in the graph -> runtime inserts a sync (cudaEventSynchronize) leading to the stall.

irina: exact output from nsys (simplified):
```
Time(ms)  Op
1200      cudaGraphLaunch (stream 2)
1200.3    kernel_attn_fused_v2 (stream 2)
1200.8    <<< gap >>>
1246.0    ncclAllReduce (stream 2)  // waits on event from stream 7
1246.1    kernel_ffn (stream 2)
```

sam: so KV cache prefetch uses stream 7 (to overlap CPU->GPU copy) and records an event. If that event isn't part of the graph, the runtime enforces ordering via a blocking wait during replay.

alex: how are we creating events for prefetch? i thought we used cudaStreamCaptureModeGlobal and only capturable streams.

priya: code snippet: `cudaEventRecord(prefetch_event, prefetch_stream); cudaStreamWaitEvent(graph_stream, prefetch_event, 0);` Prefetch_stream is sometimes a per-worker pool stream that is NOT marked capturable; we lazily create it. During capture the event becomes uncapturable and causes fallback.

sam: that would explain intermittent nature: sometimes prefetch_stream gets reused in a capturable context, other times it's fresh/uncapturable.

irina: i also noticed kernel-selection logs around the stall: shard 0 chose attention_v2_fuse (vectorized), shard 1 fell back to attention_v1_generic. The two kernels have slightly different launch semantics and create different dependencies in our wrapper (workspace alloc timing).

alex: can we force prefetch to use a capturable stream during capture? or move prefetch copies into the graph capture region so the event is recorded inside the graph?

priya: quick patch idea: when `use_cuda_graphs` is enabled, create a dedicated capturable prefetch stream per device and use it for memcpyAsync + eventRecord. Also ensure kernel selector picks deterministic variants across TP shards for same batch shape.

sam: note: making prefetch capturable might increase graph size and memory, but should preserve overlap without sync. Another option: drop StreamWaitEvent and instead enqueue the prefetch copy before capture or rely on dependency-chaining via captured memory ops. Both need testing.

irina: i ran an experiment locally: forced capturable prefetch stream -> no stalls in 200 runs. Also logs show NCCL latency stable ~3-6ms.

alex: sweet. but let's validate with variable seq lengths and mixed kernel selector. Could still get mismatch if selector yields different kernels per shard.

priya: next steps: 1) PR to create capturable prefetch streams gated on use_cuda_graphs (small change) 2) Add audit in kernel selector that emits a per-batch fingerprint to trace so we can detect cross-shard mismatches in CI 3) Add a perf test that runs 1000 iterations with graphs on to catch flake.

sam: add NVTX markers for `kv:prefetch`, `graph:capture:start/stop`, `nccl:allreduce` so traces make root-cause obvious.

irina: i'll open the PR for capturable prefetch (w/ perf numbers) and add the NVTX changes. Will also add a CI job that runs the graphs stress test on dedicated infra (lower rate but long runs).

alex: ack. if anyone hits this and needs a quick revert, flip `USE_CUDA_GRAPHS=false` in CI.

perf-bot: Regression alert: recent kernel-selector change (CL 4321) increased graph-related stalls from 0.3% -> 3.7% in nightly runs. Traces linked: https://perf.redwood/internal/graphs/1800500000/failures

irina: thanks perf-bot. PR incoming, will ping when ready for review. :thumbsup:

priya: FYI adding this to backlog with priority P1 for next sprint since it impacts production stability for Dedicated clusters.

sam: thanks everyone — good catch on the stream/event interaction.

irina: leaving logs and nsys snapshot in the thread link: https://storage.redwood/incidents/cg-nccl-stream-race/1800500000.nsys

alex: will follow up on kernel-selector gated determinism.

irina: closing note — lesson learned: cudaGraph + external events are subtle. prefer capturable-only primitives during capture or explicitly record everything inside the graph.
